newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM's Shotton to up de-inking capacity.
newsitem.headline: UPM's Shotton to up de-inking capacity.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy said in a statement on Thursday its British subsidiary Shotton Paper Company would invest about 280 million markka to double its de-inking capacity.
After the investment, recycled fibre would account for over 60 percent of the mill's raw material needs, UPM-Kymmene said.

The annual capacity of Shotton Paper's two newsprint machines is about 470,000 tonnes, or over 20 percent of consumption in Great Britain, it said. The mill would need over 400,000 tonnes of waste paper per year as raw material.

"The investment will extend the company's capability to use recycled paper to satisfy up to two thirds of its fibre requirement," UPM said adding the pulp need would be met with virgin fibre from forests and residues from sawmills in Britain.
